content: A spider lays eggs, and these eggs develop into new spiders. The term biogenesis is also used to describe the principle that living matter can only originate from pre-existing living matter. This concept stands in contrast to the hypotheses of abiogenesis, which propose that life can emerge from non-living matter under certain conditions, although the exact nature of these conditions remains unknown. Until the 19th century, it was widely believed that life could spontaneously arise from non-living matter under specific circumstances, a process referred to as spontaneous generation. This belief was largely based on common observations, such as the appearance of maggots or mold on exposed organic material, which seemed to arise without any apparent source of life. However, subsequent scientific discoveries demonstrated that, in all such observed cases, life only arises from the replication of other living organisms. A secondary meaning of biogenesis was introduced by the French Jesuit priest, scientist, and philosopher Pierre Teilhard de Chardin. He used the term to describe the origin of life itself as a result of an inherent drive in matter toward higher levels of consciousness. This idea was an extension of the now-disproven hypothesis of orthogenesis. The empirical findings of Louis Pasteur and others were summarized in the Latin phrase Omne vivum ex vivo (or Omne vivum ex ovo), which translates to all life from life (or all life from an egg). This principle, sometimes referred to as the law of biogenesis, demonstrates that modern organisms do not spontaneously arise from non-living matter in nature. It is important to note that the law of biogenesis should not be confused with Ernst Haeckel's Biogenetic Law. No cellular life has ever been observed to originate from non-living matter. While there have been reports of the construction of viable viruses capable of infection and evolution from abiotic materials, significant debate persists regarding whether viruses should be considered truly alive. Additionally, various experiments have been conducted to explore the possibility and potential mechanisms of abiogenesis.
